sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama – United States Trade Promotion Agreement (2012), including the Investment Chapter
Panama – United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT, as amended; Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 18 of 2012 and Law 21 of 2017; Law 254 of 23 July 2021 establishing the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Registry; Executive Decree 400 of 14 April 2022 regulating the UBO Registry.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución), including the Articles of Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Foundation Charter as recorded in the Public Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resident Agent's Acceptance Certificate and Registered Office Declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague counterparties)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Natural Persons / UBO Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama, upon confirmation by the compliant resident agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the Foundation Council members, officers, and every natural person holding 25% or more beneficial interest against Panamanian National Security lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified in accordance with Law 23 of 2015 and FATF Recommendations 12, 24 and 25; enhanced due diligence applies where any PEP is involved. Screening is performed by the resident agent before incorporation and thereafter on a continuous risk-basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Online Name Reservation System (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre en Línea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must contain the phrase 'Private Interest Foundation' or the Spanish equivalent 'Fundación de Interés Privado'. Names may be in any language written in Latin script; non-Latin script names must be phonetically transliterated into Latin characters. The Spanish version of the name is controlling for registry purposes, and any English version must be a faithful transliteration or translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name identical or phonetically indistinguishable from an existing registered entity
Words implying sponsored participation of the Republic of Panama or any state organ
Profane, misleading, or contrary to Panamanian public order and good morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a Recurso de Reconsideración with the General Directorate of the Panama Public Registry within five (5) business days of notification. If the reconsideration is denied, a Recurso de Apelación may be submitted to the Third Chamber (Administrative Chamber) of the Supreme Court of Justice in accordance with Law 38 of 1999. While an appeal is pending, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation under a modified name without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a substitute for the statutory registered agent. The Private Interest Foundation must maintain a resident agent in Panama with a physical office; a virtual or serviced office is acceptable solely as the address of the resident agent, provided the resident agent retains verifiable physical premises. For the target cross-border e-commerce fulfillment activity (ISIC 5210), a pure virtual address without resident-agent physical substance will not satisfy statutory registration under Law 25 of 1995.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified probability for a Low_Risk_Standard e-commerce fulfillment foundation; estimated annual risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Panama Public Registry or the UBO Registry supervision unit is less than five percent (5%). The likelihood increases to moderate if sanctions or AML anomalies are detected during ongoing compliance monitoring.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fee for the public deed of incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry incorporation filing and registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent first-year acceptance and registered office fee
UBO registry filing and PEP/sanctions screening dossier preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Resident agent or licensed compliance provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of the public deed and supporting incorporation documents (four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama or delegated apostille office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish-to-English translation of the foundation charter
External legal due diligence and incorporation supervision

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley 49 de 2000, Articles 3, 6, 10, 18 and 23; residual support from Ley 32 de 1927 (Corporations Law) where not inconsistent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Panama Public Registry, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación y Estatutos (Foundation Charter and By-laws), registered in the Foundations Folio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of US$10,000.00 (or equivalent value in lawful assets) declared in the Foundation Charter; the endowment may be fully or partially contributed within one year of incorporation. No escrow or bank segregation account is required under Panamanian law; the Registered Agent maintains the foundation's capital ledger.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at a meeting of the Foundation Council duly convened at the registered office, that: (1) the initial endowment of US$10,000.00 subscribed under the Foundation Charter is accepted and entered in the foundation accounts; (2) the registered office located at the office of the Resident Agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama, is adopted as the statutory domicile; (3) the officers named in the Foundation Charter are confirmed and appointed, namely the President, the Secretary, the Foundation Council members and the Protector; (4) the Resident Agent is retained as custodian of the statutory records, minute book and corporate seal; and (5) the President and Secretary are jointly authorized to execute and submit the Charter and By-laws to the Public Registry of Panama and to perfect all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Foundation Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (via licensed Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed Registered Agent to conduct a name availability search in the computer index of the Public Registry, then draft the Foundation Charter and By-laws in Spanish stating the foundation's name, ISIC 5210 cross-dock e-commerce fulfillment objects, US$10,000 endowment, initial council members, Protector and Resident Agent. Validate the charter against the mandatory content requirements of Article 6 of Ley 25 de 1995.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder's passport or national ID
Utility bill or bank reference evidencing founder's residential address
Draft Foundation Charter and By-laws
Name availability certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is found to be deceptively similar or reserved, file a corrected name request with the Registry and pre-reserve three alternate names to avoid delay; if the name reservation lapses, re-apply with a fresh availability search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Foundation Charter and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange the physical appearance of the founder and the appointed council members before a Panamanian Notary Public; the notary legalizes signatures, verifies identity documents, and attaches the notarial certification to the Foundation Charter and By-laws.
required_dossiers: Executed Foundation Charter and By-laws
Original identification documents of founder and council members
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary notes defects in capacity or identification, cause the signatories to re-execute before the same or another notary; pay a single new notary fee if re-execution is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Registration at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Authorize the Resident Agent to present the notarized Foundation Charter and By-laws, together with the Registered Agent's acceptance certificate and the registry fee payment receipt, before the Foundations Section of the Public Registry; follow up with the registry examiner until the foundation folio and complete Inscripción are issued.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter and By-laws
Registered Agent acceptance certificate
Registry fee payment receipt from Banco Nacional de Panamá or DGI e-pago
Registry filing request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any preventive note (nota preventiva) issued by the registry examiner within 10 business days by amending the capital or object clause as directed; pay the revised tariff and re-file the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC) and Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply in person or electronically to DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), register withholding obligations, and file an Aviso de Operación for the Panamanian physical office; where all e-commerce fulfillment income is generated abroad, claim the territorial-source exemption on the application and present written justification.
required_dossiers: Certified folio certification from the Public Registry
RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único)
Copy of notarized officers' appointments
Registered office lease or occupant authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI issues an observation on the declared activity, resubmit the RUC application with the certified registry folio and specify the territorial income source; if the Aviso is rejected, correct the activity code to ISIC 5210 and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice and Commercial Patent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama — Municipal Revenue Directorate (Dirección de Rentas Municipales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For any physical premises maintained in Panama, obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación and commercial patent from the Municipality of Panama by declaring ISIC 5210 as the activity code; pay the municipal patent and stated-capital taxes according to the municipal tariff schedule.
required_dossiers: Municipal patent application form
RUC certificate
Public Registry certificate of registration
Copy of premises title or lease contract and fire insurance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pay any undisputed municipal patent arrears, submit the payment receipt and request tax clearance; if the tariff classification is disputed, file a written reconsideration plea before the Municipal Revenue Directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certified Copies, Apostille and Corporate Kit Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and Apostille Section, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request certified folio copies and the official Minute Book from the Registry through the Resident Agent; for cross-border banking and counterparty verification, apostille certified charter extracts at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and assemble the standard corporate kit comprising seal, council minute book, charter copies and certificates of good standing.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Written request letter for apostille and certified copies
Payment receipt of registry and apostille fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the apostille is refused, first legalize the document before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or through the notary chain, then re-request the apostille; if corporate kit items are defective, order replacement certified copies from the Public Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias, MICI) — Logistics and Foreign Trade Directorate, with municipal jurisdiction vested in the Municipality of Panama
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral industrial or manufacturing permit applies to ISIC 5210 warehousing; only the municipal Aviso de Operación (Operating Notice) is required when physical premises in Panamanian territory are maintained

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Control de Calidad Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental), no full EIA report required for low-impact covered cross-dock and logistics warehouse premises without hazardous processes
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with D.E. No. 0851-2006 wastewater effluent limits: pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 400 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L for sanitary and storm-water discharge to municipal collectors; solid waste segregation and delivery to licensed operators under the National Solid Waste Regulation; negligible VOC emissions due to indoor dry-goods handling and absence of chemical processes; noise and dust control applicable around loading bays.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire prevention certificate issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá covering evacuation plan, extinguishing systems and occupational fire load; structural load inspection certificate from a registered civil engineer for racking and mezzanine installations; workplace health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) for any Panama-based staff, including forklift operations and ergonomic handling protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — General Directorate of Revenues of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Principal tax administration and e-filing portal: 'Sede Electrónica' of the DGI, accessible via dgi.mef.gob.pa, supporting the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), Aviso de Operación, ITBMS declarations, corporate income tax returns and the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) e-invoicing platform.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a conventional central bank. Monetary and banking oversight is allocated to the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá), with Banco Nacional de Panamá acting as fiscal agent and clearing channel for public deposits and USD-denominated liquidity. Exchange policy and coordination are facilitated through the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Superintendency of Banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US dollar is legal tender in Panama; the Panamanian balboa circulates only as a unit equivalent at 1:1 with the US dollar but has no independent paper supply. Full convertibility exists on both current account and capital account transactions. Profit remittance, capital repatriation and dividend distributions are free from prior exchange approvals, reserve requirements, or statutory conversion restrictions. Banks apply only ordinary AML/KYC due diligence and may report wire transfers meeting statutory thresholds to the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement for export proceeds in Panama. Exporters are not required to repatriate or convert foreign currency within a specified timeline. Cross-dock and third-party logistics revenue in USD or other foreign currencies may be retained in overseas settlement accounts or credited freely to Panamanian dollar-bearing accounts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-to-High for payment collection, virtual account issuance, and supplier settlement through cross-border electronic money institutions such as Airwallex, provided settlement is ultimately routed through a licensed Panamanian bank. Legal constraints include the absence of an independent electronic-money institution license regime in Panama; digital payment and wallet services are typically structured through supervised bank partnerships. An EMI is appropriate as an operational clearing rail, not as a substitute for the primary Panamanian bank account holding capital escrow and operational treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier-1 Panamanian banks require a general corporate onboarding interview. Physical presence of the PIF founder, council members, or authorized signatories is commonly mandated for the initial KYC discussion, unless a pre-existing private banking relationship permits remote video authentication. A notarized and apostilled power of attorney, certified copies of the foundation charter and Public Registry filing, and a valid registered agent certificate are required. Remote opening is not uniformly available and should not be assumed for a newly established Private Interest Foundation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore PIF with undisclosed beneficial owners or nominee council members
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete foundation deed and charter; updated registered beneficial ownership declaration; registered agent sworn certificate identifying founder and council members; apostilled passport pages of all economically exposed individuals; Public Registry certificate of foundation existence; corporate organizational chart demonstrating non-resident ownership legality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of demonstrable economic substance in cross-dock and overseas 3PL operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Panama warehouse lease or sublease; cross-dock equipment inventory; third-party logistics agreements with e-commerce merchants; ISIC 5210 and NAICS 493110 business definition; projected shipment volumes; customs broker engagement letter; payroll or local contractor records if staff are present in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual expected wire pattern with high cross-border velocity and repetitive USD flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy memo describing stage-4 clearing rails; platform settlement statements from e-commerce marketplaces; customer and supplier lists; written board resolution naming authorized signatories; bank reference letter from existing financiers; transaction volume forecast with monthly reconciliation methodology; AML compliance manual and transaction monitoring responsibility matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade and sanctions exposure from international shipping lanes and multimodal logistics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/sanctions screening policy; denied-party screening reports; bill of lading and cargo manifests for representative shipments; commercial invoices and packing lists; shipping carrier compliance terms; trade transaction review log; sworn certification that no transacting counterparty is a sanctioned person or entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection should be executed by SWIFT MT103 in USD from the shareholder or affiliate treasury to the Panamanian PIF's capital escrow account at a Tier-1 bank. The wire settlement details must state 'Capital contribution – Private Interest Foundation' and reference the approved board resolution. No central bank authorization is required, but the receiving bank will conduct source-of-funds verification; supporting documents include the capital contribution subscription, foundation deed, Public Registry certificate, and identity documents of the remitter. Wires above USD 25,000 may require a sworn source-of-funds statement. Remitter and beneficiary legal names must match bank KYC records exactly; use the same legal name in the ordering bank and beneficiary bank data fields to avoid exception processing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursement rails are structured as follows: supplier and freight payments settle via SWIFT MT103 with clearly populated beneficiary financial institution, account number and SWIFT/BIC codes; larger purchase order transactions may use commercial letters of credit under UCP600 issued by a Tier-1 Panamanian bank or a corresponding international bank; local operational costs such as warehousing labor and trucking are paid through Panama's local electronic clearing system aligned with Local_ACH rails; Airwallex virtual accounts are used for segregated merchant receivable collection and vendor payout in supported jurisdictions. Every outbound instruction must pass OFAC and internal sanctions screening; counterparties listed on restricted party lists are denied. The PIF must maintain an that is unexplained wire monitoring and reconciliation of each MT103 or clearing batch against the corresponding cross-dock order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions (USD versus EUR, GBP, CNY, CNH, BRL, MXN and other operational currencies)
FX forward outrights with licensed Panamanian banks or their international affiliates for USD receivables and payables hedging up to 12 months
Cross-currency swaps for multi-currency balance sheet exposure and financing translation risk
Plain vanilla FX options and collars for structured treasury risk management
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in Latin American currencies where local deliverable markets are restricted, subject to ISDA and credit support annex documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation franchise tax payment (Tasa Anual / Impuesto de Franquicia de Fundacion de Interes Privado) remitted by the Panamanian registered agent together with the DGI e-Tax consolidated payment form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July. Initial payment: by 31 July of the incorporation year for foundations formed 1 January through 30 June; by 31 January of the following year for foundations formed 1 July through 31 December. Thereafter the recurring annual payment is due each 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% surcharge (recargo) plus moratory interest at approximately 1% per month; the foundation is flagged 'en mora' in DGI records; the Registro Publico and DGI refuse to issue good-standing certificates (Paz y Salvo), blocking bank renewals, notarized amendments, and registry filings. Sustained default for three or more consecutive annual cycles exposes the foundation to administrative strike-off or removal from the Registro Publico and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership registry declaration and annual confirmation (Declaracion de Beneficiario Final), including RUUC taxpayer-data consistency check, submitted through the DGI e-Tax portal by the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Owner Registry module and Registro Unico de Contribuyentes (RUUC), Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial registration within 30 days of foundation formation; each change in the foundation council, protector, beneficiary vested-rights schedule, or asset and contribution structure must be reported within 30 days; annual data reconfirmation is consolidated by the registered agent with the 31 July franchise-tax cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an infraction under Panama AML rules (Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 129 of 2020); administrative fines up to USD 50,000 may be assessed, and the foundation is blocked from obtaining Paz y Salvo and from registering subsequent foundation acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaracion Jurada de Renta / ISLR) - nil or exemption position for foundations deriving only foreign-source income from the overseas 3PL cross-dock order-fulfilment operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax portal, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the year following the calendar tax year for foundations having Panamanian-source taxable income. A pure offshore PIF without Panama-source income is not required to file a substantive income tax return; the registered agent records the territorial-exemption position at the annual compliance cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing penalties range from USD 300 to USD 5,000 plus 10% surcharge and monthly moratory interest; false or misleading declarations attract fines of 10% to 25% of the omitted tax. These penalties apply only where a filing obligation actually arises; an entirely foreign-source 3PL foundation has no Panamanian-source chargeable event.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: 0% on foreign-source income; 0% on qualifying SEM regional headquarters income (Law 41 of 2007); reduced/zero taxation on Colon Free Zone and Panama Pacifico operations; standard domestic CIT 25% subject to the 4.567% CAIR alternative minimum tax on gross taxable revenue; PIFs also pay a flat annual fee of USD 300 (USD 350 if paid after 30 June).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 - Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas (Corporate Income Tax Return); filed electronically through the DGI E-Tax 4.0 portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, dgi.mef.gob.pa) using the PIF's RUC registration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly advance payments (1/12 of prior-year tax) with each instalment due by the 20th of the month for taxpayers whose prior-year tax exceeded USD 50,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year. A nil declaration is still required for any RUC-active PIF with no taxable Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and legal denomination of the Private Interest Foundation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Overseas PIFs with no Panama-source activity are not required to obtain a RUC; a PIF operating a Panama cross-dock must first register. Foreign parent company IDs are not accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period covered (start and end dates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar year is the default; non-calendar year requires prior DGI authorization and consistent reporting of all monthly advances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income of Panamanian source (ingresos brutos de fuente panameña)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare cross-dock, storage, fulfilment, and handling fees for services physically performed in Panama. Fees for services rendered entirely abroad (e.g., overseas warehouse operations) are foreign-source and excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt and non-taxable income (ingresos exentos y no gravables)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source 3PL revenue and overseas e-commerce fulfilment fees billed to the foreign affiliate are reported here only as informational entries; retain contracts, bank records, and warehouse location evidence for audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses (costos y gastos deducibles)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local wages, warehouse rent, utilities, transportation, depreciation, insurance, and subcontract fees paid to unrelated local carriers. Cross-border related-party charges require arm's length documentation and Form 190 filing when above the transfer-pricing threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (renta neta gravable) after absorbing prior-year losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward limited to five years; no group consolidation or absorption of foreign parent or affiliate losses.
Apply the 25% rate to Line 6; the resulting amount is compared with the CAIR alternative minimum tax on Line 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CAIR alternative minimum tax: 4.567% of gross taxable Panamanian-source revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with no RUC are not subject to CAIR; once the PIF declares Panama-source gross revenue, the higher of Line 7 and Line 8 is the final tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits applied (anticipos mensuales, retenciones de terceros) and balance payable/refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only the monthly advance payments made under the E-Tax payment schedule; no foreign tax credit is allowed because foreign income is excluded rather than taxed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign payments annex and transfer-pricing information statement (pagos al exterior y declaración de precios de transferencia)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany payments to the overseas e-commerce parent or freight affiliates (management, software, royalties, logistics fees). Form 190 must be attached when related-party transactions exceed PAB/USD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the foundation council (Consejo de la Fundación) or appointed fiscal representative/CPA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Signature of a resident CPA is advisable where the PIF has Panama-source operations; the registered agent (agente residente) certifies the foundation's legal existence and BO registry compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of USD 50 to USD 5,000 per declaration; late payment: statutory 10% recargo on the unpaid tax plus 1% monthly interest; omitted revenue triggered by inspection: fine of 10% of the omitted tax; repeated non-filing permits DGI ex officio assessment on presumed income and closure of the establishment; wilful evasion is referred to the criminal courts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed from taxed Panamanian profits; 15.5% where distribution is sourced from taxed profits not fully subject to corporate income tax or from reserved/exempt profits; distributions by a Private Interest Foundation to beneficiaries are not subject to Panamanian income or dividend withholding tax (Law 25 of 1995).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited (in force treaties with the UK, South Korea, Mexico, Qatar, UAE, Barbados, and a few others; no DTA with the US). To obtain reduced rates, the beneficial owner must (1) hold a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the counterparty tax administration; (2) submit the TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, and DGI relief form to the Panamanian payer before the payment date; (3) have the payer apply the treaty rate at source or file a refund within the statutory prescription period; (4) provide Spanish translations and keep records for five years. Hybrid entities such as PIFs are subject to enhanced DGI scrutiny on treaty residence; treaty access depends on each DTA's residence article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is generally exempt from Panamanian WHT; royalties and technical/IT service fees sourced in Panama bear a 12.5% gross-basis WHT (final corporate tax) unless reduced by an applicable DTA; excessive interest paid to related parties can be recharacterized as constructive dividends or disallowed under transfer-pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB/USD 1,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Form 190 TP information return and Local File documentation; when related-party transactions exceed PAB/USD 3,000,000, a full TP study should be contemporaneously prepared and retained; Master File documentation is recommended for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above OECD thresholds though Panama has not separately codified the Master File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's territorial system is reinforced by the Economic Substance Legislation (Law 254 of 2021) requiring taxpayers earning Panamanian-source income from relevant activities - including distribution and logistics services - to maintain local premises, adequate employees, operational direction, and actual activity in Panama proportionate to revenue. A PIF operating the ISIC_5210 cross-dock and overseas fulfilment hub in Panama must show warehouse premises, local staff, payroll, and management decisions in Panama; a letterbox PIF with no local substance risks recharacterization of revenue, denial of deductions, fines up to PAB/USD 100,000, and reassessment of up to five years. The USD 300 annual foundation fee does not by itself constitute economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Panama-source cross-dock and fulfilment revenue on Form 120, issuance of false 3PL invoices to foreign affiliates, or manipulation of the CAIR computation to understate gross taxable revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of one to three times the evaded tax plus imprisonment of up to five years; civil reassessment with the 10% recargo, 1% monthly interest, and disallowance of deductions for the fiscal period; DGI closure of the warehouse facility for repeated defaults.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, the founder-beneficiary, and the fiscal representative are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes and surcharges; criminal conviction carries travel bans, asset freezes, and surrender of passports; the foundation veil is pierced as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure (Law 254 of 2021)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing Panamanian cross-dock and overseas fulfilment fees through a PIF that has no warehouse premises, no local employees, and no operational control in Panama; claiming foreign-source exclusion for services actually performed in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to PAB/USD 100,000; loss of all deductions and incentive regimes; re-assessment under presumed-income rules for up to five years; cancellation of the foundation registration for persistent default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing permits collection from the founder's personal assets; registered agents and resident directors face professional sanctions and fines for certifying false substance declarations; the DGI may refer the case to the Public Ministry for false-tax-return offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Breach (Law 23 of 2015, as amended)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF's payment rails (Local ACH, Airwallex, Wire) to commingle merchant sales proceeds with logistics fees, processing settlement flows on behalf of unlicensed e-commerce merchants, or concealing the ownership of the overseas warehouse cash flows from the UAF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 5 to 10 years (up to 15 in aggravated cases), confiscation of the laundered assets and ancillary profits, fines of up to double the value of the funds, plus administrative sanctions imposed by the UAF and the Superintendency of Banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Real beneficial owners and foundation council members face arrest warrants, travel bans, and extradition exposure; the foundation's separate personality is disregarded for laundering instruments; directors executing suspicious transactions with knowledge are prosecuted as accomplices and ordered to pay civil restitution.
